newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Macraes a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Macraes a buy.

text.p: Broking house Wilson HTM Ltd said it was recommending gold miner Macraes Mining Ltd as a buy, reflecting the group's excellent exploration potential.
"Buy. On a price-earnings basis Macraes looks fully valued but we believe this overlooks the exploration potential," Wilson director, resources research, Phil Hutchings said in a report.
Macraes had the seventh biggest gold reserves of any Australian-Papua New Guinea gold company, Hutchings said.
"We believe it highly likely that additional discoveries should be forthcoming over the next few years," Hutchings said.
Hutchings said the Macraes gold project in New Zealand's South Island was going well with production for 1996 likely to exceed the 130,000 ounces target.
"It is possible that the 1996 year's production could be 135,000 ounces," he said.
Senior management had been strengthened following the decision to treble mill capacity to nine million tonnes annually and lift gold production to up to 350,000 ounces a year, he said.
"Macraes is aiming to have the (mill) project completed between June and December, 1998," Hutchings said.
Macraes was targeting some higher grade ore early in the life of the expansion, Hutchings said.
"The aim is to produce 350,000 ounces for the first two years at a cash cost of A$360 an ounce. Thereafter production will reduce to 320,000 ounces a year," he said.
Life-of-mine cost was forecast at A$405 an ounce, Hutchings said.
Macraes was also switching its emphasis to finding shallower and/or high grade ore which would provide lower cash costs, he said.
The group's recent Golden Bar discovery, six km to the south was encouraging, Hutchings said.
From drilling to date, he estimated that about three million tonnes at between two and three grams a tonne had been identified.
This mineralisation sat on a separate shear zone, about two km to the east of the main Macraes shear zone "raising considerable additional exploration potential," Hutchings said.
